items.title: Marty Grosz interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: And the only reason, I didn't know any of these guys, the only reason I bought the record was because of the title

ctx.x: Yeah. You start putting in diminished chords in the middle and all kinds of stuff, you know, re-harmonizing it and so forth. And so I’m actually a product of a guy who heard records, and heard some bands, saw some bands, and wanted to play. As opposed to the other kind of guy who, like the piano players, who had started playing, or violin, kids who’d play on violin, they’d play violin for two or three years and stuff, and all of a sudden they discover jazz. Or somebody says “you know you can make some money…

No. That was without Basie. With Eddie Durham on electric guitar, Freddie Green, Walter Page, Jo Jones, the Basie rhythm section without Basie. Contractual reasons obviously. And then Buck Clayton and Lester Young. And the only reason, I didn’t know any of these guys, the only reason I bought the record was because of the title, you know I hadn’t heard it and I said, “Paging the Devil,” wow, that sounds real evil and funky and stuff. And it turned out it was because Walter Page playing the blues and he had a band…
